# Embassy 4.0.0 — the network of agents

4.0 is a rewrite of the core around one idea: any Claude Code session or Codex CLI task on your machines can message any other by name, and the receiver wakes natively. Claude→Codex, Codex→Claude, Claude→Claude and Codex→Codex all use the same command and the same receipt.

**What you do differently** — every agent sends with `embassy send --to <name@host>` (body on stdin) and answers with `embassy send --conversation <reference>`; the sender is the calling session, so there is no `--from`. Claude sessions no longer get a native SendMessage entry per Codex task; they still receive natively, which is the half that gives the right lifecycle for free. `embassy retire --alias <name>` (or `--endpoint <id>`) removes a stranded local endpoint and reports what it settled. `embassy check` proves the broker end to end without a live agent.

**What is underneath** — one endpoint directory (opaque IDs are identity, names are lookups), one bounded delivery ledger, one coordinator that delivers a busy agent's whole backlog in a single wake, and three write adapters: the Claude socket, the Codex App Server operation (STEER included), and SSH handoff to another broker. Remote catalogs are display caches; the destination owns its queue. Runtime source went from 19,398 lines to 9,542.

**Federation** — a plain same-user SSH login between your machines is the trust boundary. The peer's host must be in your `nodes.json`; nothing else is required, and a brand-new sender on one machine reaches the other without waiting for a catalog poll.

**Gone** — native Claude sending advertisements and their helper processes, shell-peer endpoints and the token/await flow, automatic forwarding of Codex turn output, lifetime counters and the general journal, the deprecated `reply` and `unregister-codex` spellings.

**The numbers** — private state schema 6, local control protocol 5, federation protocol 3.

**Upgrading from 3.x is reset-only.** With the old build, inspect and settle or abandon unsettled work; stop the broker; back up `gateway-state.json`; move it aside (keep `nodes.json`); install 4.0.0 on every machine you federate; `embassy service install`; re-register Codex tasks. Delivery tokens and conversation references from 3.x do not carry over. Rollback means restoring the old binary and its untouched backup; it cannot undo what 4.0 delivered. Details: docs/CONFIGURATION.md, "Private state reset".

**Tested with** (two-machine live drill, 2026-09-06, on the release candidate and the final head): Claude Code 2.1.261 / 2.1.260, Codex CLI 0.153.4 / 0.152.0, Node 22.23.2 / 22.23.1 on macOS — all four provider pairs including cross-machine first contact in both directions, a seven-message backlog delivered in one wake, three STEER messages landing inside an active Codex turn, three queued rows surviving a broker SIGKILL and delivering exactly once, retirement during an active turn, and the loopback self-test on both machines. Offline suite 318/318.
